question: What is the primary physical change that happens first in a joint affected by osteoarthritis?

options.D: Fusion of the two bone ends

explanation: Osteoarthritis starts when the protective cartilage covering the ends of bones begins to wear away and break down. [learn more](GNS222_U1_T14#GNS222_U1_T14_h1)

question: Why do bony spurs, or osteophytes, form around a joint with osteoarthritis?

options.A: Muscles pull too hard and stretch the bone outward
options.B: Infection causes new bone cells to multiply rapidly
options.C: Calcium supplements settle directly into the joint space
options.D: The body tries to spread out weight load after losing cartilage

explanation: As cartilage wears away and bone rubs on bone, the joint attempts to heal itself by growing bony spurs to help support the extra pressure. [learn more](GNS222_U1_T14#GNS222_U1_T14_h1)

question: What is the single biggest risk factor for developing osteoarthritis?
explanation: Getting older is the primary risk factor because joint cartilage naturally weakens and loses its shock-absorbing ability over time. [learn more](GNS222_U1_T14#GNS222_U1_T14_h2)

question: How does carrying excess body weight contribute directly to knee osteoarthritis?

options.A: It increases mechanical stress on weight-bearing joints and promotes inflammation
options.B: It stops the body from producing normal synovial fluid
options.C: It causes the leg muscles to weaken and shrink away completely
options.D: It blocks calcium from reaching the bone ends inside the joint

explanation: Extra weight forces the knee joints to bear heavier loads with every step, and fat tissue also releases chemicals that trigger joint inflammation. [learn more](GNS222_U1_T14#GNS222_U1_T14_h2)

question: What is the typical pattern of pain experienced in the early stages of osteoarthritis?

options.A: Sudden sharp pain that only happens during deep sleep
options.B: Severe constant pain that never changes day or night
options.C: Pain that worsens with activity and gets better with rest
options.D: Pain that disappears completely when walking long distances

explanation: Early osteoarthritis pain is typically triggered by joint use and eased when the client rests the affected limb. [learn more](GNS222_U1_T14#GNS222_U1_T14_h3)

question: How can you tell the difference between morning joint stiffness in osteoarthritis versus inflammatory arthritis?

options.A: Osteoarthritis stiffness only affects the upper body joints.
options.B: Osteoarthritis stiffness never happens in the morning hours.
options.C: Osteoarthritis stiffness usually lasts less than thirty minutes.
options.D: Osteoarthritis stiffness gets worse the more the person moves.

explanation: Joint stiffness from wear-and-tear arthritis is brief after waking up, whereas inflammatory arthritis causes stiffness lasting an hour or more. [learn more](GNS222_U1_T14#GNS222_U1_T14_h3)

question: Which imaging test is most commonly used to confirm a diagnosis of osteoarthritis?
explanation: X-rays are the standard and most cost-effective way to view joint space narrowing and bone spurs characteristic of osteoarthritis. [learn more](GNS222_U1_T14#GNS222_U1_T14_h4)

question: Why do doctors order blood tests such as ESR or CRP when evaluating a client with joint pain?

options.A: To rule out inflammatory arthritis or other systemic conditions
options.B: To measure the exact amount of cartilage left inside the knee
options.C: To check if the client has an active vitamin D deficiency
options.D: To track how fast the bone spurs are growing every month

explanation: Because osteoarthritis does not raise inflammatory blood markers, normal blood tests help rule out other forms of arthritis like rheumatoid disease. [learn more](GNS222_U1_T14#GNS222_U1_T14_h4)

question: What is a major advantage of using topical NSAIDs instead of oral NSAIDs for older adults with osteoarthritis?

options.A: They never require a prescription from a doctor
options.B: They work within seconds to stop all joint swelling
options.C: They completely reverse the loss of joint cartilage
options.D: They have fewer systemic side effects like stomach ulcers

explanation: Topical NSAIDs deliver medicine directly to the painful joint through the skin, avoiding the high bloodstream concentrations that cause gastrointestinal bleeding. [learn more](GNS222_U1_T14#GNS222_U1_T14_h5)

question: Why are corticosteroid injections into an arthritic joint typically limited to only a few times a year?

options.A: The body quickly builds up an absolute immunity to the drug
options.B: Steroids instantly dissolve all the remaining bone spurs
options.C: Frequent injections can cause further damage to the joint cartilage
options.D: The medication permanently stains the skin around the joint

explanation: While steroid shots relieve inflammation fast, repeated use over time can actually weaken and break down the remaining cartilage inside the joint. [learn more](GNS222_U1_T14#GNS222_U1_T14_h5)

question: Which type of physical activity is generally best recommended for a client with knee osteoarthritis?

options.B: Low-impact exercises like swimming and cycling
options.C: Complete bed rest to avoid any joint movement
options.D: High-impact sports like running and basketball

explanation: Low-impact activities strengthen supporting muscles and lubricate the joint without placing crushing stress on the damaged cartilage. [learn more](GNS222_U1_T14#GNS222_U1_T14_h6)

question: When should a nurse teach a client to apply cold packs rather than heat to an arthritic joint?

options.A: Right before starting a long walk or stretching routine
options.B: After physical activity when the joint feels swollen and inflamed
options.C: Only when the weather turns very cold outside
options.D: First thing in the morning when the joint feels stiff

explanation: Cold helps constrict blood vessels and numb acute swelling after use, whereas heat is better for relaxing stiff muscles beforehand. [learn more](GNS222_U1_T14#GNS222_U1_T14_h6)

question: What is the primary surgical goal of joint arthroplasty for a client with severe hip osteoarthritis?

options.A: Permanently fusing the hip bones together so they can never move again
options.B: Clearing out loose debris with a tiny camera without touching the bone
options.C: Cutting the thigh bone to shift body weight away from the damaged area
options.D: Replacing damaged bone and cartilage with artificial components to relieve pain

explanation: Arthroplasty involves total joint replacement where worn surfaces are swapped for artificial parts to restore pain-free movement. [learn more](GNS222_U1_T14#GNS222_U1_T14_h7)

question: Why is arthrodesis (joint fusion) rarely performed on major weight-bearing joints like the knee or hip today?

options.A: It requires the client to stay in bed for an entire year.
options.B: It causes severe allergic reactions in most clients.
options.C: It makes the joint grow back larger bone spurs within weeks.
options.D: It permanently eliminates all movement in that joint.

explanation: While fusion successfully stops pain, losing all joint mobility makes walking and normal daily activities extremely difficult. [learn more](GNS222_U1_T14#GNS222_U1_T14_h7)

question: Which complication is a major risk for clients taking long-term oral NSAIDs for osteoarthritis pain?

options.A: Sudden uncontrollable weight loss and high fever
options.B: Rapid overgrowth of new joint cartilage
options.D: Permanent darkening of the skin and hair

explanation: Oral NSAIDs block protective stomach lining chemicals, putting regular users at high risk for ulcers and bleeding. [learn more](GNS222_U1_T14#GNS222_U1_T14_h8)

question: A client taking daily ibuprofen for knee osteoarthritis tells the nurse they noticed dark, tarry stools. What is the nurse's best action?

options.A: Tell the client to drink more water and double their daily walking distance
options.B: Suggest that the client switch to taking the pain pill on an empty stomach
options.C: Instruct the client to stop the ibuprofen and report the finding to the provider immediately
options.D: Explain that dark stools are a normal side effect of all joint medications

explanation: Dark, tarry stools indicate upper gastrointestinal bleeding, a serious complication of NSAID use that requires immediate medical attention. [learn more](GNS222_U1_T14#GNS222_U1_T14_h8)
